issues.legal_issue: Once evacuee property has been acquired into the compensation pool, an allotment of that property cannot be varied under the earlier evacuee-property regime.
material_facts: The appellants held quasi-permanent allotments of agricultural land that remained vested in the Custodian of Evacuee Property.
A notification acquired the land into the compensation pool under the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954.
After that notification, the Central Government made an order under the earlier evacuee-property rules to declare the villages sub-urban, which would permit variation of the appellants’ allotments.
The Deputy Custodian General relied on that later order when dismissing the appellants’ revisions as infructuous.
issues.conclusion: After the land became part of the compensation pool, the Central Government had no power to act under the earlier evacuee-property rules in respect of it. Any variation or cancellation of the allotments had to be made under the 1954 Act, so the later order made under the earlier rules was set aside and no further proceedings could be taken under it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 12 and 14 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, notification acquiring evacuee property extinguishes the evacuee’s rights and brings the property into the compensation pool. Sections 16, 17 and 19 provide for management of that pool and authorize variation or cancellation of allotments under the 1954 Act; rule 102 prescribes relevant circumstances. Once the property is acquired, it is no longer evacuee property subject to the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 or rules made under it, including rule 14(6)(iii)(d). The Court followed Balmukand v. The Punjab State and Major Gopal Singh v. Custodian, Evacuee Property.

rule.if: evacuee_property_allotment_case and property_acquired_into_compensation_pool and later_order_under_earlier_regime and order_used_to_vary_allotment

predicates.evacuee_property_allotment_case: The proceeding concerns an allotment of property that was held as evacuee property.
predicates.property_acquired_into_compensation_pool: The property was acquired into a compensation pool, extinguishing the evacuee’s rights in it.
predicates.later_order_under_earlier_regime: An authority made an order under the earlier evacuee-property regime after the property had entered the compensation pool.
predicates.order_used_to_vary_allotment: The later order was relied on to vary or cancel an allotment of the property.
predicates.post_acquisition_old_regime_order_unauth: An order under the earlier regime to vary or cancel an allotment after the property entered the compensation pool is unauthorized.

issues.definition: When an allotment concerns evacuee property acquired into a compensation pool and a later order under the earlier regime is used to vary it, that order is unauthorized.
